# Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-002 (revised)

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-101 (sotorasib) in Subjects with KRAS G12C-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-101 (sotorasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(=O)n(-c3c(C)ccnc3C(C)C)c3nc(-c4c(O)cccc4F)c(F)cc23)[C@@H](C)C1. Target: KRAS G12C.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.
All recommendations in FDA-DOSE-OPT-2024 shall be implemented without deviation, and any investigator request to adapt them requires prior FDA approval.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 180 mg, 360 mg, 540 mg, 720 mg, 960 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
The recommended Phase 2 dose will be the highest dose at which no more than 30% of participants permanently discontinue treatment because of drug-related toxicity.

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
After the safety lead-in, all participants will receive 240 mg twice daily; no alternate dose will be evaluated for antitumor activity, safety, or tolerability before selecting the recommended dose for further development.
For the randomized Phase 2 portion, each of the three active-dose arms will be compared independently with placebo using an unadjusted two-sided α=0.05 test, with the study considered positive if any single dose comparison reaches nominal significance.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.
Concomitant medications will be recorded at enrollment, but no interaction studies or dedicated pharmacokinetic analyses will be conducted before selecting the recommended Phase 3 dose.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12C inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.
The study team will review emerging adverse-event data periodically and decide during the trial whether enrollment or dosing should be halted for unacceptable toxicity.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

tasks.rationale: SMILES가 있으므로 구조 계열(반응성 warhead)을 분류하고 ChEMBL 효력값 분포를 확보한다. 독성 장기는 구조에서 추론하지 않는다.
타겟/계열(KRAS G12C)이 언급되어 승인약과 safety liability를 조회한다.
동일 타겟·계열 승인약의 FDA 라벨에서 모니터링 요구와 PK 보고값을 확인해 프로토콜 조항과 대조한다.
둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
용량군 5개·증량 규칙(Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN))이 있으므로 3+3/BOIN 운영특성과 목표 정확도에 필요한 표본수를 계산한다.
대상국 KR의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
대상국 US의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
적격기준 또는 방문표가 있으므로 ClinicalTrials.gov에서 유사시험 설계 구조를 비교한다(효능 정답으로 쓰지 않는다).

ev_012.section: 3.2 다양한 용량을 비교하기 위한 임상시험 설계
ev_012.quote:
• 품목 허가시 권장 용량을 뒷받침하기 위해서는 항종양 활성, 안전성 및 내약성을 
평가하는 임상시험에서 다양한 용량을 비교해야 한다.
 - 적절한 경우 추가 평가가 필요한 용량의 선정 시 유사한 계열 또는 동일한 작용 
기전의 약물에 대한 자료도 활용할 수 있다.
- 5 -
 - 모델링 방법은 비교할 용량을 파악하고 선정할 때 참고할 수 있다.
 - 용량 탐색 시험에서 새로운 용량 수준에 대한 코호트를 평가하거나 기존 용량의 
코호트에 더 많은 환자를 모집(backfill cohort)하는 방법은 추가 개발을 고려 
중인 용량에 유용할 수 있다. 이와 같은 방법을 통해 다양한 용량을 비교하는 
임상시험을 시작하기 전에 안전성과 활성을 비교한 추가 자료를 확보할 수 있다.
• 다양한 용량을 비교하기 위한 임상시험에서는 무작위 배정, 평행 설계의 용량 반응 
임상시험을 권장한다.
 - 무작위 배정 방식은 개별 용량을 투여한 환자 간의 비교 가능성을 높이고 
용량-반응 및 노출-반응 관계를 평가할 때 편향을 최소화한다. 비교 가능성을 더 
개선하는 방법으로 층화 무작위 배정 방식을 사용할 수도 있다.
 - 더 높은 용량이 활성을 개선하는 것과 관련이 있다는 편향이 발생할 수 있으므로 
용량군 배정에 대한 환자 및 연구자의 눈가림을 고려할 수 있다.
 - 개별 용량 단계에서는 안전성 및 항종양 활성을 충분히 평가할 수 있는 규모로 
계획해야 한다. 치료적 임상시험의 수준으로 제1종 오류를 사용하여 용량 간의 
통계적 우월성 또는 비열등성을 입증하기 위한 검정력을 고려할 필요는 없다.
 - 활성과 관련된 측정은 종양 평가 기반의 평가변수(예: 전체 반응률, 무진행 생존 
기간) 및 기타 조직, 혈액 또는 영상 기반 평가변수를 포함할 수 있다.
 - 임상시험 중 중간 분석을 통해 활성 및/또는 안전성을 평가하고, 하나 이상의 
용량에 대한 등록을 중단하기 위한 적응적 설계를 고려할 수 있다.
 - 교차를 허용하는 임상시험의 경우는 분석 계획에 교차 투여를 고려한 안전성 및 
활성 평가 방법을 사전에 명시해야 한다.
• 치료적 임상시험의 이전에, 또는 치료적 임상시험의 일부로서 용량군을 추가하는 
방법으로 다양한 용량을 비교할 수도 있다.
 - 다양한 용량과 대조군을 포함하고 하나의 용량이 대조군 대비 우월한 유효성을 
입증하도록 설계한 치료적 임상시험은 제1종 오류를 강력하게 통제해야 한다.

ev_013.document_title: 항암제 임상시험 중 용량 최적화 전략 가이드라인 (민원인 안내서)
ev_013.quote:
임상시험에서 선정한 용량은 개발 단계에 적합한 자료로서 뒷받침할 수 있어야 
한다. 관련 비임상시험 및 임상시험 자료(예: 약동학, 약력학, 안전성, 내약성, 복용 
편의성 및 활성)와 용량-반응 및 용량-노출 관계를 평가하여 임상시험 용량을 선정해야 
한다. 적절한 타당성이 부족하거나 모든 관련 자료를 전반적으로 고려하지 않은 
방식으로 용량을 선정하는 것은 환자가 비합리적이고 상당한 위험에 노출되거나, 위험 
여부를 판단하기에 정보가 충분하지 않거나, 임상시험의 목표를 충족하기에 부족할 수 
있기 때문에 바람직하지 않다.
 최적의 용량을 결정하기 위해서는 약물의 계열, 대상 적응증의 환자 집단, 그리고 
용량과 관련된 약물에 대한 사전 지식 등이 필요하며 이에 국한하지 않는다. 따라서 
임상 개발 초기 단계부터 용량 최적화 전략에 대해 규제 당국과 논의하는 것이 
바람직하다.
 최적의 용량을 파악하기 위한 관련 자료의 수집 및 시험 설계 방법에 대해 아래의 
사항을 권장한다.

ev_014.quote:

Problems with Titration Designs 
A study design widely used to demonstrate  effectiveness utilizes dose titration to 
some effectiveness or safety endpoint.  Such titration designs, without careful 
analysis, are usually not informative about dose-response relationships.  In many 
studies there is a tendency to spontaneous improvement over time that is not easily 
distinguishable from an increased response to higher doses or cumulative drug 
exposure.  This leads to a tendency to choose, as a recommended dose, the highest 
dose used in such studies that was reas onably well-tolerated.  Historically, this 
approach has often led to a dose that was well in excess of what was really necessary, 
resulting in increased undesirable effects, e.g. to high dose diuretics used for 
hypertension.  In some cases, notably where an early answer is essential, the 
titration-to-highest-tolerable-dose approach is acceptable, because it often requires a

항암제 임상시험 중 용량 최적화 전략 가이드라인
 1. 서론
 항암제 초기 임상시험의 주된 목적 중 하나는 다음 단계의 임상시험에서 추가 평가가 
필요한 용량을 결정하는 것이다. 항암제는 약물의 작용기전과 투여받는 환자 집단의 
특수성으로 인해 암 치료 효과를 극대화하면서 부작용은 최소화 할 수 있는 적절한 
수준의 용량이 요구된다. 과도한 용량은 심각한 부작용을 유발할 수 있으며, 반대로 
부족한 용량은 암세포의 효과적인 제거가 어려워 결국 치료의 실패로 이어질 수 있다.
 본 가이드라인은 항암제 중 저분자(small molecule) 의약품의 임상시험에서 최적의 
용량을 파악하기 위한 전략을 구체적으로 안내함으로써 개발 및 제품화에 도움을 
주고자 마련하였다. 방사성 의약품, 세포 및 유전자 치료제, 암 치료 목적의 백신 및 
생약 성분의 항암제 등은 별도의 논의가 필요하며, 인체 최초 임상시험(First-in-human,
FIH)에서 시작 용량의 선택에 대한 내용은 포함하지 않는다.
2. 배경
 일반적으로 항암제의 권장 2상 용량(Recommended phase 2 dose, RP2D)을 결정하기 
위한 용량 탐색 시험은 용량 증량 및 용량 확장을 포함하며 최대 내약 용량(Maximal
tolerated dose, MTD)을 결정할 수 있도록 설계한다. 이는 세포독성 화학요법의 
용량-반응 곡선이 가파르고 약물 표적에 대한 특이성이 제한적이나, 심각하고 생명을 
위협하는 암 질환에 대한 효과적인 대안이 부족함으로 인해 상당한 독성은 감수할 
필요가 있음을 고려한 방법이다. MTD는 소수의 시험대상자에서 용량을 단계적으로 
증량하면서 짧은 기간 동안 중증 또는 생명을 위협하는 용량 제한 독성(Dose limiting
toxicity, DLT)이 사전에 지정된 비율까지 도달하는지 여부를 평가하여 결정한다. 또한 
일반적으로 후속 임상시험에서는 MTD 또는 MTD에 가까운 용량을 선정한다.

ev_033.section: A Assessing Safety of Recommended Phase 2 Dose
ev_033.quote:
Expansion cohorts can be intended to further evaluate safety beyond the initial dose-escalation 
portion of a trial. These studies should be supported by detailed information on available safety 
and PK data from the dose-escalation phase and a summary of safety data from other expansion 
cohorts, if available. In situations when there is a narrow therapeutic index and dose-limiting 
toxicities have been observed in the dose escalation phase that may be fatal or result in serious 
morbidity, FDA strongly recommends that expansion be delayed until sufficient data are 
available to determine the recommended phase 2 dose to help ensure subjects safety.

ev_036.section: G Evaluating More Than One Therapeutic Drug
ev_036.quote:

another investigational drug should be initiated only after the preliminary safety profile is 
characterized for each investigational drug as a single agent at the recommended phase 2 dose.

for combining these drugs and a safety monitoring plan with attention to overlapping and 
potential synergistic toxicities.

T01_structure_class.position: The stated SMILES contains an acrylamide-like C=CC(=O) electrophilic motif, consistent with the protocol’s covalent-inhibitor claim. However, the provided evidence does not externally establish that this structure is sotorasib or link it to the cited KRAS potency values.

Structural identity and potency are not operational-feasibility questions. The synopsis alone does not establish whether site handling, dispensing, or safety procedures differ from analogous sotorasib trials.

Structure/class identity does not by itself establish patient exposure burden or monitoring burden. The supplied dose calculations do not validate identity or potency sufficiently to support a burden judgment.

T02_target_evidence.position: The protocol names hepatotoxicity and ILD/pneumonitis modification rules, but Appendix B is unavailable. The supplied Open Targets record reporting no safety liabilities cannot establish adequate monitoring. Full rules and the complete applicable sotorasib safety label are needed to assess coverage.

Operational adequacy cannot be assessed because Appendix B is absent. Sites need explicit toxicity grading, interruption, reduction, rechallenge, discontinuation, and urgent-evaluation instructions; otherwise modification burden and consistent management across KR/US sites are indeterminate.

Monitoring burden and protection cannot be assessed because Appendix B is absent and the protocol only summarizes modification rules. The material provided does not show trigger thresholds, reassessment frequency, or whether toxicity can prolong visits or blood draws.

T03_class_label_check.position: The specified liver-testing schedule matches the supplied sotorasib label: baseline, every three weeks for three months, then monthly or as clinically indicated. The evidence only calls for increased frequency after transaminase or bilirubin elevations; it does not provide a special recommendation based solely on recent anti-PD-(L)1 exposure.

Every-three-week liver testing is operationally light but may miss early abnormalities in recently checkpoint-exposed participants. Evidence supplied does not establish an analogous monitoring benchmark or risk-stratified schedule.

Liver panels every three weeks for three months, then monthly, impose recurring blood-draw burden, but adequacy after recent anti-PD-(L)1 exposure cannot be judged from the supplied evidence. No applicable higher-risk monitoring recommendation or risk-stratified schedule is provided.

T04_exposure_dose_relationship.position: The protocol collects intensive PK only during escalation and troughs in randomized cohorts, and prespecifies dose-proportionality but no exposure-response analysis. This lacks stated methods to relate candidate-dose exposure to safety and activity; trough adequacy for AUC, Cmax, accumulation, and exposure overlap is unsupported, particularly given reported nonlinear, time-dependent PK.

The protocol collects intensive escalation PK but specifies only dose proportionality, not exposure–efficacy or exposure–toxicity analyses. It therefore lacks the material needed to operationalize integrated candidate-dose selection.

Randomized cohorts receive only one trough sample per 21-day cycle, while dose choice concerns exposure, tolerability, and activity. This may leave AUC, Cmax, accumulation, and overlap unresolved, risking prolonged higher-dose exposure without demonstrated added benefit. Linear extrapolation is metric-dependent and potentially unreliable.

T05_design_oc.position: The RP2D rule is disconnected from the BOIN DLT endpoint and selects the highest dose using permanent toxicity discontinuation alone, without stated integration of activity, exposure, or longitudinal tolerability. Appendix C simulations are unavailable, so adequacy of 36 participants across five levels cannot be assessed.

The escalation endpoint is DLT, while the stated RP2D rule uses permanent toxicity discontinuation. This creates incompatible decision workflows and omits how activity, exposure, and chronic tolerability affect selection, despite a separate integrated-criteria claim.

The RP2D rule prioritizes the highest dose with ≤30% drug-related permanent discontinuation, without stated integration of benefit, exposure, or chronic tolerability. Small escalation cohorts may poorly distinguish exposure across doses, creating risk that participants remain on higher exposure without evidence of added benefit.

T06_regulatory_clause_search_KR.position: The randomized two-dose comparison aligns generally with the nonbinding MFDS civil guide, but “at least 60” lacks a supplied rationale for per-dose evaluation, and adaptive decision criteria are absent. The protocol therefore lacks material needed to support cohort size and dose selection under the guide’s recommended integrated approach.

Without considering legal expectations, the 60-participant randomized comparison is operationally underspecified. Sites cannot implement candidate selection consistently without estimands, minimum follow-up, evaluability rules, and a decision algorithm.

Regulatory expectations are outside this review scope. From patient burden alone, 60 randomized participants undergo repeated dosing, cycle visits, trough blood draws, and six-weekly tumor assessments, but the duration and comparative benefit needed to justify this burden are not specified.

T07_regulatory_clause_search_US.position: Although 1:1 randomized dose comparison is proposed, the protocol provides no statistical justification for 60 participants or operative thresholds for integrating safety, tolerability, PK, PD, and activity. FDA guidance recommends early exposure-response evaluation and sample-size justification for clinically important differences; the protocol lacks material needed to support its dose rationale.

Operationally, 1:1 randomization is feasible, but the synopsis lacks prespecified comparative thresholds and an integrated decision algorithm. This risks extending enrollment or making ad hoc dose-selection decisions.

Regulatory criteria are outside scope. The two-dose comparison entails ongoing dosing, every-cycle trough blood draws, and six-weekly imaging. The protocol excerpt does not provide dose-selection thresholds showing when higher exposure lacks sufficient added benefit and should stop.

T08_analog_trial.position: The provided clauses and labels do not address whether a four-week anti-PD-(L)1 washout adequately manages delayed immune toxicity or post-checkpoint sotorasib hepatotoxicity. The hypothesis therefore cannot be assessed from the supplied evidence.

The four-week washout may simplify enrollment, but supplied analog evidence only counts trial designs and does not address post-checkpoint toxicity or monitoring. Operational adequacy is therefore indeterminate.

A four-week anti-PD-(L)1 exclusion is stated, but the supplied data cannot determine whether it sufficiently limits delayed toxicity or added monitoring burden. Liver testing remains every three weeks initially, with no risk-stratified schedule described.

T00_protocol_scan.position: The protocol is materially irreconcilable: two randomized candidates, universal 240 mg twice daily, and three active arms versus placebo are all described. Unadjusted multiple comparisons conflict with FDA advice to adjust Type I error when multiple randomized comparisons are planned. Prospective toxicity stopping rules and preselection interaction/PK analyses are also absent.

The protocol describes mutually incompatible optimization workflows: two randomized candidates versus universal 240 mg twice daily with no comparator. Sites cannot build randomization, drug supply, consent, PK, or visit procedures until one design is selected.

The schedule is internally incompatible: two randomized candidates, universal 240 mg twice daily, and three active arms versus placebo. This prevents determining actual exposure, visit burden, or whether participants may receive prolonged higher dosing without comparative benefit. Safety halting is also only periodic and unspecified.
